title: T1496.001 — Resource Hijacking - Compute Hijacking
subtitle: This simulation shows a complete compute hijacking attack on a Kubernetes cluster.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Finding the exposed dashboard
steps.caption: The attacker scans the internet for Kubernetes dashboards, which are web control panels for clusters. One dashboard answers without asking for a password. The firewall sees ordinary scan noise, so no alert fires
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

fields.detail: The attacker scans the internet for Kubernetes dashboards, which are web control panels for clusters

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Creating a privileged pod
steps.caption: The attacker uses the dashboard to send API calls that create a pod with full host privileges. A pod is a group of containers that runs together. The audit log records the creation, and the caller is anonymous - the first strong signal
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Pulling the miner image
steps.caption: The pod downloads a public miner image, a ready-made mining program packaged for containers. A service account with no history pulls a Monero miner at 2:41 a.m. The cluster now runs attacker code

steps.title: Scaling to more pods
steps.caption: The attacker copies the pod to every node, so all cores work for the same wallet. Twenty similar pod creations in forty minutes, all from one source IP, reveal the scale-out

steps.title: Defender signals align
steps.caption: The SOC joins three weak signals: anonymous pod creation, the CPU plateau, and egress to a pool address. The correlation rule raises one critical alert with full context. This is the CH-04 plus CH-02 join from Section 5, with node CPU metrics adding the third signal
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Containment
steps.caption: The SOC evicts the miner pods, moves the dashboard behind the VPN (virtual private network - a private remote-access path), and rotates exposed tokens. Pool sessions end and CPU returns to baseline within minutes
